content: The Multnomah County Sheriff's Office Search and Rescue (MCSO SAR) is a non-profit organization composed of volunteers that provides search and rescue services for the Multnomah County Sheriff's Office in Oregon, United States. This organization also extends its services, which amount to 3,000 to 5,000 volunteer hours annually, to other counties in Oregon, including Clackamas, Columbia, Washington, Marion, Hood River, Wasco, Tillamook, and Clatsop, as well as Skamania and Clark counties in Washington. MCSO SAR was established in 1961 in collaboration with the Boy Scouts of America and is recognized as one of the longest continuously operating Explorer Search and Rescue units in the United States. In 1986, the sponsorship of MCSO SAR was transferred to the Multnomah County Sheriff's Office. The organization is also a member of the Mount Hood Search and Rescue Council. Training All members of MCSO SAR undergo extensive training in various disciplines, including first aid, legal aspects of search and rescue, emergency survival skills and equipment, radio communications, land navigation, GPS orientation, crime scene safety and security, search organization and management, search techniques, man tracking, helicopter safety, wilderness medicine, and rescue techniques. While the state mandates a minimum of 40 hours of training annually, MCSO SAR requires its members to complete 200 hours of training each year. This additional training includes rope rescue techniques, rope and pulley systems, urban search and rescue scenarios, response to terrorist attacks, natural disasters, urban searches, crime scene evidence searches, and snow and avalanche safety. MCSO SAR also participates in the Washington State Search & Rescue Conference annually, where members receive specialized training in various subjects. Starting in the summer of 2007, the organization introduced optional training programs that include advanced topics such as high rope rescue, advanced first aid, advanced survival skills, and helicopter training. Services MCSO SAR provides critical services to Multnomah County, Oregon. Its members serve as the primary first response team for locating missing, lost, or injured individuals within the county. They are frequently called upon by other counties to assist in large-scale search operations or when resources are depleted. Additionally, MCSO SAR members often conduct crime scene evidence searches at major or outdoor crime scenes across Oregon and have been credited with solving hundreds of homicide cases. Beyond emergency response, MCSO SAR members contribute to public safety by organizing and participating in events aimed at educating the public about outdoor safety. They also assist with various public events by providing services such as security, parking/traffic management, and first aid. For example, MCSO SAR recently provided security for the LPGA Golf Tour held at the Columbia Edgewater Country Club in Portland, Oregon. Membership Requirements To become a member of MCSO SAR, individuals must meet several criteria: Be at least 14 years old and maintain a GPA of 2.5 or higher. Pass a criminal background check. Have up-to-date vaccinations. Be physically capable of prolonged periods of hiking and standing. Maintain a minimum amount of required outdoor equipment and clothing. Be available on-call 24/7. Pass a state certification exam. Other Agencies Several other agencies assist with search and rescue operations in Multnomah County, including: Portland Mountain Rescue (PMR) American Medical Response Reach & Treat Team (AMR RAT team) Pacific Northwest Search & Rescue (PNW SAR) Mountain Wave, which provides communications and radio support AMR River Rescue Search-One K9 Washington County Explorer Search and Rescue Clackamas County Search and Rescue Mt.
